Run Sheet

One page. Everything else in this intermission is commentary.

DayBeatThe one thing that must happen
6The Fallow Ford — 6 ankhegs, 2,700 XPKeep the visibility tally. Nothing else here is load-bearing.
12@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GradJrnl000]{Gradsul quay}Roke says the fire rule out loud. One sentence, on his deck, in front of the players.
12–15@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GullJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GuPgGM00000]{The Gull's Job} (optional)Nothing. It costs no days, and the Kestrel Wife sails on Day 15 whatever happens; the worst it can do is move her to the evening tide.
29The Grey Fee — 2,850 XP on the party's sideThe count in round two: “Five! Count 'em — five, and no burning!” Then the circular reaches them by one of four routes.
31@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GBckJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GbPgBay0000]{The crew's superstition}Somebody says a grey-back follows a bloody hull. Roke tells them to stow it.
37The Grey-Back — 3,150 XPWick Ferrin goes over the rail in round one. The hull track starts.
40Hardby, duskHand off to @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.phase-3-journals.JournalEntry.BR2P3ArrivalJrnl.JournalEntryPage.BR2P3ArPgArr02Cmm]{Arrival — Commercial Cover} with two lines adjusted — see the hand-off page.

Read-alouds. Every encounter carries its own, on its own pages, and five montage pages carry the days between: @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1FordJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1FdPgRoad000]{The Road South (Days 1–5)} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1FordJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1FdPgKeol000]{Into Keoland (Days 7–11)} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GFeeJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GfPgVoyage0]{Out to Sea (Days 15–28)} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GBckJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GbPgBay0000]{Woolly Bay (Days 30–36)} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GBckJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GbPgLast000]{The Last of the Bay (Days 38–40)}. The per-PC beats, all in one place: @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1QRefJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1QrPgBeats00]{Per-PC Narration Beats}.

Scenes

@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnFord0000]{The Fallow Ford} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnTunnel00]{The Ankheg Tunnel} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnBoard000]{The Kestrel Wife, Boarded} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnSea00000]{The Kestrel Wife at Sea} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnGrad0000]{Gradsul, City Map (GM)} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnMuse0000]{Gradsul, The Royal Museum} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnMerm0000]{Gradsul, The Mermaid's Inn} · @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnMermUp00]{The Mermaid's Inn, Upstairs}

The clocks, all in one place

ClockLengthWhat it costs
The cart (Ford)3 roundsWool samples ruined. Three days and 140 gp in Gradsul, and letters that no longer match the cargo.
The berth (Grey Fee)3 roundsThe decoy strongbox is taken. The real package is sewn into a bale.
The slow-match (Grey Fee)4 rounds, then 6 segments3 segments, the forward hold is going. 6, the ship is a beacon off the Pomarj.
Heat (the Gull's Job)6 segments5, the bell-rope and the Watch in ten rounds. 6, hue and cry, and the Harbour Warden holds the morning tide.
Overboard (Grey-Back)2 rounds per manWick Ferrin.
The hull (Grey-Back)4 segmentsSteering, then the rudder, then the pump, then a harbour that looks twice.

Stall rails

If they will not leave Gradsul: Vole's market gossip reaches them — a man has been asking after westerners who pay in Yeomanry drafts. It is true, it is vague, and it moves them onto a hull inside a day.

If they try to hire their own ship: let them, at four times the price, and put the circular in the hands of the second master they interview rather than the one they hire. The hunt does not depend on the Grey Fee; it depends on four hulls and a guess.

If they want to fight nothing: the Ford can be run past (two rounds of cart-turning and a Survival check to find the upper crossing) and the grey-back can be baited off in one round by anyone who listens to the crew. The boarding cannot be avoided, because it comes to them.

XP and the Sixth-Level Line

The party ends Phase 2 on 12,169 XP each. Sixth level is 14,000. So they need 1,831 each, which across five PCs is 9,155 XP of enemies.

BuildEnemy XPPer PCLands at
Base: 6 ankhegs + boarding as written + grey-back and three hunters8,7001,74013,909 — 91 short of 6th
+ the boarding's second wave (4 more boarders)9,1001,82013,989 — 11 short, which would be unbearable
+ second wave and a fourth hunter shark9,5501,91014,079 — 6th level at the rail

So: run both dials and they make 6th somewhere in Woolly Bay on day thirty-seven, which is where you want it — because Phase 3 is calibrated for five PCs at levels 6–7. Or ignore the arithmetic entirely and award the voyage as a milestone the way the Loftwick sessions were awarded; 2,000 each covers it with room to spare.

Gradsul. @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GullJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GuPgGM00000]{The Gull's Job} is the only XP between the Ford and the Grey Fee, and it pays at most 470 each: 170 for the brawl and 300 for the job as a milestone. With the boarding's second wave the party can hold no more than 13,829 after the Grey Fee, so it can never level them early, and any Gradsul award at all carries the base build over the line on Day 37. Never award more than 640 each in Gradsul.

Do not hand the level out on arrival in Hardby. Levelling on the deck, before the harbour, is what makes the six weeks feel like it counted for something; levelling on the quay makes it feel like a reward for turning up.

Budgets, for the record

Five PCs at 5th: low 2,500, moderate 3,750, high 5,500. All three encounters sit between low and moderate on paper and play at moderate, because each is an objective with a clock rather than a hit-point race and because this party has no front line to absorb a first exchange. Nothing here should threaten a wipe; the boarding explicitly cannot, once the count is called.

Per-PC Narration Beats — the Intermission

GM-only. Each beat goes to its player privately, in a sentence or two, and is never explained. Full threads live in @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.pc-threads.JournalEntry.BR2PcThreadsJrnl]{Per-PC Plot Threads}. Written for five: Cam is absent for this stretch (PC-01) and has none. Spotlight notes are table advice, not beats.

Alicia Trévanne — The Pact Silence

Fires at: Day 12, the Foaming Tower (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GradJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GrPgCity000]{Into Gradsul}); Day 29, in the middle of the boarding (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GFeeJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GfPgAfter00]{Aftermath}).

The beats: at the tower she reaches for her patron out of habit, the way every hand in the port reaches for Osprem, and gets the same distant attentiveness as in Loftwick: alert, listening, saying nothing. In the boarding she reaches again, in the middle of a fight, for the first time — and gets the same.

Also hers: on a Mixed tally the circular's line is about her blade, and Vole has told the Gradsul market about it. In the Mermaid's, a pact blade out of thin air is still a blade.

Kitty Raleigh — Chthonic Recognition

Fires at: Day 12 (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GradJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GrPgCity000]{Into Gradsul}, then @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GradJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GrPgShip000]{The Kestrel Wife}); Day 29 (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GFeeJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GfPgAfter00]{Aftermath}).

The beats: nobody in Gradsul looks twice at a tiefling, the first time since Loftwick; on the Kestrel Wife's plank an old hand steps out of her road and touches the iron of the rail. On Day 29 Mattick Sarn looks at her once, properly, and then makes a point of not looking again.

Spotlight: spike growth or entangle at the Ford; the grey-back is hers, the only creature aboard who can meet it in its own element (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GBckJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GbPgRules00]{Underwater Rules}).

Gianni Varren — Geographic Erasure

Fires at: Day 9, a crossroads (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1FordJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1FdPgKeol000]{Into Keoland}); Day 15, the prow (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GradJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GrPgSail000]{Out of the Sheldomar}); Day 29, the Grey Fee's chart case (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GFeeJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GfPgAfter00]{Aftermath}).

The beats: a milestone with the arm naming an old waystation recut away, the chisel marks still pale, the same work as the Loftwick waymark. The bow rail where nobody can scrape the sea off a chart, and she lets her shoulders down. Then a coastal chart with two anchorages scraped out and redrawn, in the same hand as the recut waymark.

Spotlight: Survival free at the Ford; Sev and her accent; clean shots from the tops on Day 37.

Ellyndra “Elle” Swiftfoot — The Sealed Records of Her Order

Fires at: Day 12, Wick's offer (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GradJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GrPgShip000]{The Kestrel Wife}); Day 19, the lesson (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GFeeJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GfPgVoyage0]{Out to Sea}); Day 29, Tarrow's crossbow (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GFeeJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GfPgAfter00]{Aftermath}).

The beats: Wick Ferrin decides she will pick up splicing fastest, and teaches her on Day 19. On Day 29, the lightning bolt of Heironeous has been filed off Tarrow's crossbow stock, badly, and recently; there is no good answer to where he got it. If the margin-note beat from her thread has not fired yet, any temple library in Gradsul will do.

Spotlight: the only one who fits the ankheg tunnel; a fist-fight with no blades allowed at the Mermaid's; one moment out along the sweep with nothing under her on Day 37.

Selvara Stormborn — Dreams of Cut Stone

Fires at: the first night out of Gradsul, Day 15 (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GradJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GrPgSail000]{Out of the Sheldomar}).

The beat: the stair comes back — the same torchlight, the same seventh step, the same mark she cannot focus on. Nothing new. The sea does not keep it away.

Also hers: Roke's fire rule is said to the whole table and aimed at her, and he remembers who broke it; on a Loud tally the circular's line is about her. Tell her the underwater fire rule before she picks a spell on Day 37, not after.

Hand-off to Phase 3

Two lines of the canon arrival want adjusting

@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.phase-3-journals.JournalEntry.BR2P3ArrivalJrnl.JournalEntryPage.BR2P3ArPgArr02Cmm]{Arrival — Commercial Cover} still runs almost unchanged, which is the point of building the intermission this way. Two sentences want a hand.

“The harbour takes you in without a flicker” — if the hull track reached segment 2 or worse, it takes them in with one flicker: the customs boy counts bales, and then walks aft and looks at the repairs, and asks what happened, and writes down whatever they tell him. He still does not count faces. But there is now a piece of paper in a Hardby harbour office with their story on it, which Phase 3's Pressure Clock may want later.

“You have learned the smell of raw fleece in a wet hold” — let that sentence carry the rest of it: the Grey Fee's dead, a fortnight of pumping, and the hand they got back or didn't.

The two lines, written out

Read these in place of the canon sentences as you read the arrival. The first only if the hull track reached segment 2 or worse and the party has no weigh-ticket from the Gull; the second in whichever version fits.

[In place of “…and the harbour takes you in without a flicker … He does not count faces.”] Hardby comes up on the starboard bow at dusk on the fortieth day, and the harbour takes you in with a single flicker: a forest of masts, a fouled tide, a customs boy who boards at the mole and counts bales — and then walks aft, and looks for a long moment at the patched rail and the sprung rudder, and asks what happened to her, and writes down whatever you tell him. He does not count faces.

[In place of “You have learned the smell of raw fleece…”, hull at segment 3 or 4:] You have learned the smell of raw fleece in a wet hold well enough that you will know it for the rest of your lives, and the clank of a pump at two in the morning.

[…if any of the crew died:] You have learned the smell of raw fleece in a wet hold well enough that you will know it for the rest of your lives, and the sound a hammock makes going over the side.

[…both:] You have learned the smell of raw fleece in a wet hold well enough that you will know it for the rest of your lives, and the clank of a pump at two in the morning, and the sound a hammock makes going over the side.

What the party carries up the Whalemarket steps

Three things they did not have in Loftwick. A circular proving they were hunted before they ever left Keoland, and that the hunt was a guess. A mark in wax tying that hunt to the loose stone on Tannery Row and to Sarth's forged writ. One initial nobody has explained.

And two smaller things worth writing on the back of the sheet: the third wharf, and trade-drafts on a Hardby house that is not Cindren & Vhal.

If they did @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GullJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GuPgGM00000]{The Gull's Job}, one more: the Gull's papers. The weigh-ticket means the customs boy writes nothing down whatever the hull track says, and the docket squares the letters with the bales if the samples were lost at the Ford. Both put the canon arrival back exactly as it is written; see @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GullJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GuPgPay0000]{Payoff & Consequences}.

What must still be true when Phase 3 opens

The firm suspects and does not know. @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.phase-3-journals.JournalEntry.BR2P3ArrivalJrnl.JournalEntryPage.BR2P3ArPgGMBrief]{GM Brief — Phase 3 Purpose} is unchanged: about five weeks of alarm, no confirmation the party is in Hardby. The circular went to four masters on a guess; one of them acted on it and is now dead, sunk or fled, and nobody has reported back. If the Grey Fee escaped, that is worth one Pressure Clock segment at the GM's discretion and no more.

“E.” is one letter. Veska's reveal in @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.phase-3-journals.JournalEntry.BR2P3InvestigJrn.JournalEntryPage.BR2P3InPgVeskaR1]{The Veska Reveal — Reading the Chops} is intact and is now better, because the party is holding a copy of that initial before she explains what a hand is.

Tamsin is alive at the Whitemoor Estate, Veska is cautious, Tarsh is confrontable, and Castrian Vell is the party's host. Nothing here touches any of that.

Ledger

Findings against this intermission take the stable prefix TI1- in docs/gm-fix-ledger.md, filed after the Phase 9 block so the phase numbering stays contiguous. TI1-01 to TI1-18 were filed and closed in the v1.9.6 review pass, before it was ever run at the table; later findings follow on from TI1-19; the ledger has the next free number.

Never-Name Reminder & the “E.” Problem

This intermission puts a signed letter in the players' hands, which makes it the most dangerous document the campaign has produced so far. The guardrail, restated:

Never, on any page a player can see: Eclavdra. House Eilserv. Drow, dark elves, or any synonym. Erelhei-Cinlu. The Vault. The Underdark. Nor any inference that narrows “E.” to a person, a species, or a place.

What “E.” is allowed to be, here: a letter of the alphabet at the bottom of a circular, copied by a clerk who also does not know what it means.

Three ways a table talks itself into the reveal, and the answer to each

“Whose initial is it?” — Nobody aboard knows, including Sarn, who was told not to read the papers and is proud of having obeyed. The honest GM answer is that the party is holding the first physical evidence that the person exists. That is a lot. Let it be a lot.

“Is it a person or a house?” — The circular's own text refuses to say: not the house's name, not in your own accounts. A house with a name it will not write down, signed with one letter, is exactly as far as Phase 3 goes.

“Can we match the handwriting?” — Yes, and this is the trap worth walking into on purpose. They can match it to a Hardby clerk's copying hand, because that is what it is. The matching that matters happens in Hardby with Veska, and what it produces is a mismatch, not a name.
